no-priors.name: No Priors
no-priors.bio: Podcast: Baseten CEO Tuhin Srivastava on the AI Inference Crunch, Custom Models, and Building the Inference Cloud

html_en:
As AI agents evolve from assistants to genuine collaborators, the industry is grappling with fundamental questions about intelligence distribution, enterprise integration, and the delicate balance between capability and control.

The Infrastructure Behind AI's Next Phase

The dramatic scale-up of AI inference is revealing new truths about the technology's trajectory. Box's Aaron Levie offered perhaps the most prescient insight of the day:
"When there are 100X more agents than people, which parts of software will grow because agents are doing more work that the underlying software is tied to."
This isn't just speculation—it's already happening at companies like Baseten, which CEO Tuhin Srivastava says has grown 30x in the past year while serving the inference needs of AI-native companies. Watch/Listen: No Priors: Baseten CEO on AI Inference Crunch The growth isn't just in scale—it's in sophistication. As Srivastava explained,
"customers are realizing they can kind of own their inference more and more. As the application layer just gets bigger and bigger and bigger... we just happen to index on that."
Levie's analysis suggests this trend will reshape enterprise software entirely:
"These agents still need guardrails, security, compliance, workflows to be tied to, data stored, and so on. Those parts of the system of record ecosystem will only go up over time."

Agents as Collaborators, Not Employees

A fascinating philosophical shift is emerging in how builders relate to AI systems. Zara Zhang captured this beautifully:
"I realized a lot of people treat coding agents as their employee, whereas I actually treat it as my cofounder. I don't just give orders. I present problems, describe the situation, and ask for their opinion."
This mindset is being validated by real product developments. Peter Steinberger was effusive about Codex's new goal-setting feature:
"The new /goal feature in codex slaps."
The excitement around these collaborative interfaces suggests we're moving beyond simple command-response patterns toward genuine AI partnership. Sam Altman's casual return to Twitter with
"man its good to be back on twitter. there is comfort in the skills of a wasted youth"
hints at OpenAI's confidence in their position as this collaborative future unfolds.

Enterprise Reality Check

While Silicon Valley focuses on cutting-edge capabilities, Levie offered crucial perspective on actual enterprise adoption:
"When I talk to enterprises outside of Silicon Valley, most of the use-cases they have in mind with AI are to augment and accelerate how they work, simply because of how much more they can do right now."
This aligns with Baseten's customer data showing that
"if you look by inference count, it'd be 99% the [application companies]. And that kind of represents the scope of the opportunity here is that the majority of the market hasn't come online and added AI into the system."
The gap between hype and reality remains enormous, but it's closing fast. As Levie noted:
"They're also bringing intelligence to work that would have never been possible to do before. Tech jobs got concentrated in valley and the tech industry, and enterprises or SMBs have not been able to build the products or bring automation to most areas of work. AI lets them do so now."

Memory and Persistence: The Missing Piece

Claude made significant moves toward addressing one of AI's core limitations with new memory capabilities for managed agents. The feature allows agents to learn across sessions, with filesystem-based storage that developers can fully control. Early adopters are seeing dramatic results. Rakuten's agents are
"cutting first-pass errors by 97%"
by learning from past mistakes, while Netflix agents can
"carry context across sessions, including insights that took multiple turns to uncover and corrections from a human mid-conversation."
This development addresses a fundamental limitation that has kept AI systems feeling ephemeral. As agents gain persistence, they're moving from tools toward genuine digital colleagues.

The Builder's Moment

Individual builders are finding remarkable success in this environment. Nikunj celebrated reaching
"$36,500 in ARR"
with an AI-powered house hunting service built using Railway, Conductor, and Claude. Meanwhile, Replit's Amjad Masad marked the company's 10th anniversary by making the platform
"totally free for 24 hours starting at 5am PT"
in celebration of helping
"millions learn & ship."
These success stories suggest the infrastructure and tooling have reached a maturity level where individual developers can build substantial businesses—a democratization that may be the most profound impact of the current AI wave. The industry appears to be at an inflection point where the infrastructure scales, the interfaces improve, and the economic opportunities multiply. For builders willing to think of AI as a collaborator rather than a tool, the moment feels particularly ripe.
html_zh:
当代码智能体成为我们的"合作伙伴"，企业开始将AI置于工作流核心时，推理基础设施正在经历前所未有的增长。今日AI生态系统中，一些最引人注目的发展正在重塑我们与智能工具的协作方式。

推理云的狂奔：年增长30倍背后的故事

Baseten正在经历令人瞩目的增长轨迹。在最新的播客访谈中，CEO Tuhin Srivastava透露了这家推理云公司的惊人数据：

"我们在过去一年中增长了30倍...我认为我可以说今年我们预计实现超过10亿美元的收入。"

Srivastava将这一增长归功于几个关键趋势的汇聚。开源模型已经"跨越了某种基线能力的门槛"，而强化学习和后训练技术的成熟让客户意识到"他们可以更多地拥有自己的推理能力"。

更引人注目的是，尽管增长如此迅猛，按推理次数计算，99%的市场仍未上线。正如Srivastava所说："这代表了机会的规模——大部分市场还没有上线，还没有将AI添加到他们的系统中。"

观看完整访谈： No Priors播客：Baseten CEO论AI推理紧缩与定制模型

重新思考人机协作：从员工到合作伙伴

开发者们正在重新定义与AI代码工具的关系。Zara Zhang提出了一个颇具启发性的观点：

"我意识到很多人将编码智能体当作他们的员工，而我实际上将它当作我的联合创始人。我不只是下达命令。我提出问题、描述情况，并征求他们的意见。"

这种心态转变反映在OpenAI最新推出的功能上。Peter Steinberger对新的/goal功能赞不绝口，在推特上表示："Codex中的新/goal功能简直太棒了。"

但并非一切都完美无缺。Anthropic最近发布了一份详细的事后分析报告，承认Claude Code在过去一个月中确实出现了质量问题。报告坦诚地解释了三个不同的问题，包括将默认推理努力从"高"改为"中等"的错误决定，以及一个导致Claude显得"健忘和重复"的缓存优化错误。

阅读详情： Anthropic关于Claude Code质量问题的更新

AI工具的普及化：从工作场所到日常生活

Claude正在扩展其连接器生态系统，从专业工作工具延伸到日常生活应用。新增的连接器包括AllTrails、Instacart、Audible、Tripadvisor等，让用户可以在同一个对话中处理从徒步路线规划到杂货购买的各种任务。

这种扩展反映了一个更广泛的趋势：AI正在从专业工作场景渗透到我们生活的各个角落。正如Anthropic在其博客中所说："连接的应用越多，Claude能做的就越多。"

与此同时，Amjad Masad宣布Replit迎来了10周年纪念日，在推特上写道："为了庆祝，我们从太平洋时间早上5点开始，24小时完全免费。"这标志着代码学习和开发工具的民主化进程又迈出了重要一步。

了解更多： Claude日常生活连接器

企业AI应用的深层逻辑

Box CEO Aaron Levie对企业AI采用提出了一个引人深思的框架：

"未来软件的简单启发式规律是，当代理比人多100倍时，软件的哪些部分会增长，因为代理正在做更多与底层软件相关的工作。"

Levie进一步解释了企业对AI的真实需求："当我与硅谷之外的企业交谈时，他们考虑的AI用例大多是增强和加速他们的工作方式，仅仅因为他们现在能做的事情多了很多。"

这种观点得到了市场数据的支持。一位独立开发者Nikunj分享了他的AI驱动房地产分析工具已经达到36,500美元年收入的里程碑，展示了AI应用在细分市场的商业潜力。

记忆与智能的新边界

Anthropic为其Claude Managed Agents推出了内置记忆功能，让代理能够跨会话学习。Netflix、Rakuten和Wisedocs等公司已经开始使用这一功能来构建能够从每次交互中学习的长期运行代理。

正如Dan Shipper所观察到的："模型比任何个人都知道得更多，但任何个人学习得比模型更快。"

这种记忆功能的引入标志着AI代理正在从无状态工具演进为有状态的协作伙伴，能够积累经验并改进表现。

技术详情： Claude Managed Agents的内置记忆

从推理基础设施的爆炸性增长到AI工具的普及化，从企业级应用到个人生活场景，我们正在见证一个AI深度嵌入各个层面的时代的到来。关键不再是AI是否会改变我们的工作方式，而是我们如何与这些越来越智能的系统建立更好的协作关系。
